corinthians1.8.p1.b1.text: Now about food sacrificed to idols: We know that we all have knowledge.

corinthians1.8.p1.b2.text: Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up.

corinthians1.8.p1.b3.text: But the one who loves God is known by God.

corinthians1.8.p2.b4.text: … We know that an idol is nothing at all in the world, and that there is no God but one.

corinthians1.8.p2.b5.text: yet for us there is but one God, the Father, from whom all things came and for whom we exist.

corinthians1.8.p2.b6.text: And there is but one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom all things came and through whom we exist.

corinthians1.8.p3.b7.text: But not everyone has this knowledge. Some people are still so accustomed to idols that they eat such food as if it were sacrificed to an idol.

corinthians1.8.p3.b8.text: And since their conscience is weak, it is defiled.

corinthians1.8.p3.b9.text: Be careful, however, that your freedom does not become a stumbling block to the weak.

corinthians1.8.p4.b10.text: For if someone with a weak conscience sees you who are well informed eating in an idol’s temple, will he not be encouraged to eat food sacrificed to idols?

corinthians1.8.p4.b11.text: So this weak brother, for whom Christ died, is destroyed by your knowledge.

corinthians1.8.p4.b12.text: Therefore, if what I eat causes my brother to stumble, I will never eat meat again, so that I will not cause him to stumble.
